warning: CANONICAL PEAK-FCF SANITY-CHECK CASE: a prior run produced IV $22.75 (and a subsequent $7.93) by extrapolating FY2025 record-year FCF/EBITDA forward. FY2025 (Revenue $439.6m, EBITDA $95.9m, NPAT $32.0m, FCF $53.3m) was a RECORD year; FY2023 (EBITDA $26.0m, NPAT -$14.5m) was the cyclone/frost trough. FY2026 guidance (Jun-2026: NPBT $38-42m vs FY2025's $47.5m) confirms moderation is already underway. This model is built on MID-CYCLE economics (~$65-67m mid-cycle EBITDA on a component-built margin path), NOT the FY2025 peak. Base-case IV against FY2025 PEAK earnings will structurally show below-average P/E/EV-EBITDA multiples -- this is the correct, expected relationship for a cyclical valued off normalized earnings, not a modeling error. See sanity_checks block.

inputs.interest_income_strip_rationale: Seeka is a NET DEBT company (net debt $100.3m, not net cash), so interest income is not stripped from FCF -- the interest-income double-count trap only applies to net-cash companies. Net debt exceeds 1x the mid-cycle FCF base, so no interest-income adjustment is required or applied.
inputs.sbc_source: SEK.NZ_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column, cross-checked against duckdb kpis EquityAwardTaxes=0 for all years; SBC is genuinely negligible (0-$0.15m/yr across FY2015-2025, never exceeding 0.05% of revenue)
inputs.uncovered_dilution_mechanism: No share buybacks in company history. Dilution comes from the Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP) issuing new shares at a 2% VWAP discount plus historical placements (share count grew 15.0m -> 44.0m over FY2015-2025, ~11%/yr driven mostly by large one-off placements in FY2018-2019 and FY2021-2022 to fund capex/debt reduction, not ongoing SBC). Recent run-rate DRP-only dilution is ~1.5-2.0%/yr, used as the projected annual_share_growth_pct.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and FCF CAGRs are NOT meaningful for this ticker: FY2023 was a loss-making trough (EPS -$0.34, FCF -$20.1m) and FY2020-2022 FCF alternates sign, making CAGR math undefined or explosive (e.g. EPS 3yr CAGR 68% purely reflects recovery off a near-zero FY2022 base of $0.16). Revenue CAGR (8-12%) and Equity CAGR (3-11%) are usable but even these span a trough-to-peak window. Growth for the DCF was NOT selected via CAGR extrapolation; base-case revenue growth (1-3.5%/yr) reflects modest post-moderation volume growth off a mid-cycle starting revenue of $400m, informed by Zespri's 5-year industry plan (+10% trays to 2030) rather than any single historical CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is negligible (0-0.05% of revenue every year) so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF series are virtually identical -- the SBC adjustment is immaterial for this ticker, unlike SBC-heavy names. The material trap here is peak-vs-trough FCF, not SBC dilution.

mid_cycle_fcf.methodology: Component build (EBITDA -> less SBC -> less D&A -> EBIT -> x(1-tax) -> NOPAT -> +D&A -> less capex -> less/plus change in WC -> owner FCF), NOT extrapolation of any single historical year's FCF or margin. Historical raw FCF (FY2015-2023 mostly negative from orchard/post-harvest expansion capex) is explicitly NOT used as the base -- capex was expansionary, not maintenance, in those years, so negative FCF reflected growth investment rather than distress (directly analogous to the FSLR precedent).
mid_cycle_fcf.mid_cycle_ebitda_range_considered: 60-75m per task constraint; selected ~$65-67m (year-1 base-case EBITDA) sits between the straight FY2022-2025 4-year average ($61.0m) and a guidance-informed blend of FY2023/24/25 actuals + FY2026E ($69.7m implied from NPBT guidance ratio), reflecting structurally higher SunGold mix (Zespri 5yr plan: SunGold +17% to 163.5m trays by 2030) without assuming the FY2025 record repeats.
mid_cycle_fcf.rationale: The mid-cycle base-year (Yr0, pre-growth) revenue of $400m, growing to $404m in Yr1, sits below FY2025's record $439.6m (reflecting the FY2026 guided moderation: NPBT $38-42m vs FY2025's $47.5m, NZ Class 1 trays 45.4m vs record 47.1m, Australian harvest -14%) but above FY2023's trough ($300.9m). EBITDA margin path (16.5% -> 18.3% over 5yrs) sits between the FY2023 trough margin (8.6%) and FY2025 peak margin (21.8%), and above the 5-year straight-average margin (~16%), reflecting the structurally improving SunGold mix management and Zespri both flag as an ongoing tailwind.
mid_cycle_fcf.note: Base-case year-1 owner FCF ($38.4m) is materially below the FY2025 peak owner FCF ($53.2m) by design -- this is the entire point of the mid-cycle correction that this ticker's task brief specifically tests for.

premiums.description: ~60% of Seeka's revenue flows through Zespri's single-desk export mandate. Seeka has no ability to independently market kiwifruit internationally and limited pricing leverage on post-harvest service fees. Any change to Zespri's pool allocation or fee structure directly impacts Seeka with no substitutable customer base of comparable scale.

EBITDA peak/trough ratio of ~3.7x (FY2025 $95.9m vs FY2023 $26.0m) within a 3-year window, driven by weather events Seeka cannot control (Cyclone Gabrielle 2023, hot/dry 2026 season). High fixed-cost base (12 packhouses, 650+ permanent staff) amplifies the earnings swing from any given volume shortfall.

Market capitalisation of approximately NZ$218m (44.03m shares x $4.95) places Seeka firmly in NZX small-cap territory with correspondingly thin trading liquidity and a narrower investor base able to hold the position, warranting a size/liquidity premium over the broad-market NZ discount rate.

wacc_rationale.notes: Base WACC of 15.5% sits within the ~15-17% total range implied by stacking the standard NZ small-cap base (11.0-12.0%) with the three structural premiums above (minimum stack ~15.0%, maximum stack ~17.5%). Bull case uses a modestly lower WACC (14.0%) reflecting reduced weather/execution risk if the bull scenario plays out (no weather event, Australia scales); bear case uses a higher WACC (17.5%) reflecting elevated risk after a weather event materializes mid-horizon.

base.scenario_framing: Mid-cycle base case: revenue moderates from FY2025's record $439.6m to a $404m mid-cycle starting point (in line with FY2026 guidance of a lower, still-strong NPBT), then grows modestly (1-3.5%/yr) reflecting industry SunGold-driven volume growth (Zespri 5yr plan: +10% industry trays to 2030) without assuming a repeat record season. EBITDA margin improves gradually (16.5% -> 18.3%) on continuing SunGold mix shift and automation (Reemoon), staying below the FY2025 peak margin (21.8%). Cash tax rate ramps modestly (10% -> 21%) reflecting persistent horticultural/capex tax-depreciation shields evident in FY2023-2024 actuals (near-zero or refund cash tax), not a full ramp to the 28% statutory rate. Capex normalizes from a still-elevated 5.9% of revenue toward a 5.0% maintenance level as the packhouse capacity build-out (>50m tray capacity already in place) recedes.

bull.scenario_framing: SunGold volume growth continues at industry-leading pace, Australian orchard developments finally scale (2.25m kg 2026 harvest recovers and grows as new plantings mature), and no material weather event occurs across the horizon. Year-1 owner FCF ($52.2m) sits close to the FY2025 peak ($53.2m) x ~0.98, consistent with the 'no weather event' framing rather than a fresh record.

bear.scenario_framing: A weather/cyclone event lands mid-horizon (year 2, modelled on the FY2023 Cyclone Gabrielle precedent: EBITDA margin compresses to 9.0%, revenue falls 10% in that year alone) combined with ongoing Zespri pricing pressure eroding post-harvest service fee economics. Year-1 owner FCF ($22.1m) sits at ~0.42x the FY2025 peak, and the year-2 trough owner FCF ($11.1m) is well below even the FY2023 actual trough. Higher DRP-driven dilution (2.25%/yr) reflects balance-sheet stress encouraging scrip-heavy dividend reinvestment.

horizon_rationale: 5-year explicit horizon is appropriate here: base-case owner-FCF margin is roughly stable across the projection window (9.5% -> 10.6%, not still steeply ramping), reflecting SEK's status as a mature, ex-hypergrowth business now past its packhouse capacity build-out (>50m tray capacity already installed) rather than a scaling story requiring a 10-year build to reach steady state.

entry_price.methodology: Full-formula 15% IRR: (Sum FCF_t/1.15^t + TV_5/1.15^5 - net_debt) / projected_shares[5], t=1..5. TV_5 uses the scenario's Gordon/cap-bound terminal value (computed with WACC), only the discounting back to today uses the 15% hurdle. NEVER terminal-value-only.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bear.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (13.5%-17.5%), Columns = terminal growth (1.0%-3.0%). Cell = base-case intrinsic value/share. All cells use terminal value = min(Gordon, 5.5x terminal EBITDA cap); Gordon binds in every cell shown given SEK's ~50-55% FCF/EBITDA conversion ratio at these WACC levels.

valuation_philosophy.description: Seeka is best framed as an income-plus-modest-growth holding rather than a growth compounder. The dividend was fully resumed in FY2025/26 after a two-year suspension through the FY2023 cyclone trough: $0.55/share returned to shareholders over the ~12 months to April 2026 ($0.10 Jan-25, $0.05 Apr-25, $0.15 Oct-25, $0.25 Apr-26 final), fully imputed (NZ franking credits attach to the dividend, though these have no direct value to non-NZ-resident/non-taxpaying holders). Stated dividend policy targets 50-75% of underlying NPAT, implying a payout in the ~$16-24m range at the FY2025 NPAT level ($32.0m) or ~$10-16m at the FY2026 guided midpoint (~$21m NPAT, i.e. NPBT $40m less ~28% tax minus deferred tax noise). At the current price ($4.95) and a normalized 25-30c/share annual dividend, the running yield is approximately 5.1-6.1%, fully imputed. The equity case therefore combines (a) a mid-single-digit-to-high-single-digit fully-imputed dividend yield, (b) modest mid-cycle revenue/EBITDA growth from ongoing SunGold mix shift and industry volume growth (Zespri 5yr plan +10% trays to 2030), and (c) optionality from further debt reduction (net debt down from $172m in 2023 to $100.3m in Dec-2025) increasing future payout capacity -- rather than a re-rating growth story.
valuation_philosophy.dividend_normalized_range: $0.25-0.30/share (fully imputed), reflecting 50-75% of underlying NPAT at mid-cycle earnings

historical_multiples.note: FY-end (31 December close) EV/EBITDA computed on SBC-adjusted (i.e. effectively unadjusted, since SBC is negligible for this ticker) trailing EBITDA. These will NOT match Yahoo/screener GAAP multiples exactly due to differing EBITDA/net-debt definitions and timing. FY2023 is a trough-EBITDA outlier (10.9x) excluded from the 'average'/'max' figures used for scenario multiple caps.

scenario_cap_selection.rationale: Bear ~ 10yr min region (3.1-3.7x recent lows); Base ~ ex-outlier average (5.58x); Bull ~ ex-outlier max (7.9x, FY2017).

vs_fy2025_peak_earnings.note: P/E (5.97x) and EV/EBITDA (3.13x) implied against FY2025 PEAK earnings sit below the historical AVERAGE multiples (13.0x P/E, 5.58x EV/EBITDA) but well within the hard sanity ceilings (26.0x, 11.85x). This is the expected, correct relationship for a mid-cycle valuation measured against a record earnings year -- paying a below-average multiple on peak earnings is standard cyclical-stock behaviour (the Peter Lynch inversion), not a modeling flaw.

vs_mid_cycle_normalized_earnings.note: Against mid-cycle (normalized, 5-year-average) earnings rather than the FY2025 peak, implied P/E (16.6x) is modestly ABOVE the 13.0x historical average and implied EV/EBITDA (4.50x) sits comfortably within the historical 3.1-7.9x range, close to the 5.58x ex-outlier average. This cross-check confirms the base-case IV is well-triangulated to mid-cycle economics rather than either the FY2025 peak or the FY2023 trough.

fcf_quality_history.note: SBC is negligible for this ticker (never exceeding 0.05% of revenue), so reported and owner FCF are virtually identical. The material historical distortion is NOT SBC -- it is cyclicality: FY2015-2023 FCF is mostly negative from orchard/post-harvest EXPANSION capex (packhouse build-out, orchard acquisition), not distress, and must not be used as a 'normal' base. Interest income is not stripped because Seeka is a net-debt company throughout.
